World.title: In praise of Mymensingh’s Bangla folk ballads
World.content:
Folk-ballads are living archives that represent the imagination, values, ideas, and aesthetics of the people to whom they belong. Bangla literature has a rich repertoire of folk ballads. We are, however, quite oblivious of this treasure trove and, therefore, there is a dearth of research on these folk elements.

Czech Indologist Dusan Zbavitel's Bengali Folk-Ballads From Mymensingh And The Problem Of Their Authenticity can be called a wonderful exception in this regard. It is considered to be the first literary study of the beautiful folk-ballads from Mymensingh. The study was published by the University of Calcutta in 1963.

A brief background of the book may not be irrelevant here. In 1923, Rai Bahadur Dineshchandra Sen edited a volume of epic songs from the Mymensingh District of the then Eastern Bengal under the title Maimansimha-gitika. The ballads were mainly collected by Chandra Kumar De, a literary activist from the area. In the following years, Dineshchandra published three more volumes of balladic texts containing epic songs from different parts of Eastern Bengal. The beautiful ballads received enthusiastic response and admiration in India and abroad. However, for some scholars these ballads were too good, and they shared doubts about the ‍antiquity, authenticity and folk character of these lores. Dusan Zbavitel found this uncertainty "highly regrettable" and undertook a study to assign to the ballads their proper place—"one of the high points of Bengali literature". Dr Zbavitel tried to find out: "what is it that makes them so excellent?"

Zbavitel confined his analysis to the study of the ballads originating in Mymensingh—41 ballads containing more than 21,000 verses. He took an arduous effort of analysing each of these 41 ballads to prove their originality and, I must say, he achieved his goal with marked success.

One key argument put forward by Zbavitel in favour of the originality of the gitikas from Mymensingh is that these ballads are not collected by a single person and, still, there are similarities among the ballads: identical images, and similar artistic approach and common inventory of similes and metaphors. So these ballads couldn't be the creation of a modern poet as suggested by some detractors.

According to Zbavitel, the most significant aspect of these folk ballads is that they are devoid of any religious implications. They generally show harmonious co-existence of the Hindu and Muslim communities, without religious bias on either side. Zbavitel points out the fact that most of the Hindu ballads were collected from Muslim singers, which shows, according to him, that these folk poems were enjoyed and appreciated by both the communities with the same eagerness. The secular outlook of the folk ballads is diametrically opposite to the explicit religious connotation of the classical Bangla literary texts such as Mangal-kavyas and Vaisnava literature.

Zbavitel extensively discusses the ideological and artistic approach of the ballad writers, verse and rhyme technique, and use of similes and metaphors in chapter three and four of the book. The most dominant motif, according to Zbavitel, is love. Even the historical and heroic epics can be grouped into this category.

As to the literary techniques, the ballad writers, being true to the characteristics of folk epics, do not try to introduce innovations in their lyrical dictions. They are content with the poetic means offered by their predecessors. They want to tell an interesting and touching story in a simple garb, fresh with country scenes and feelings.

Zbavitel also discusses the manner of preservation of the folk ballads—preserved, in most cases, in torsos. Referring to two versions of the same ballad, Maishal Bandhu, he argues, "The 'original' ballads [were] sometimes rewritten by another folk poet, or other poets, quite freely, without any scruples; whole portions, as well as individual couplets and verses, were taken over, others were replaced by newly replaced passages, and the story itself was often changed." The reasons behind such changes, according to Zbavitel, might be an effort to offer listeners a 'better' story than the original one.

Due to this oral nature of preservation, it is always difficult to prove the originality of folk elements. If we undertake an effort to study the folklore of Bangladesh, Zbavitel's book will be an invaluable companion guide.

Rabindranath Tagore wrote to Dinesh Chandra Sen in appreciation of the book Maimansimha-gitika, "Classical Bengali literary texts such as Mangal-kavyas are ponds dug on by order and at the expense of the rich, but Maimansimha-gitika is a source of exuberance from the deepest level of the heart of rural Bengal, a clear stream of genuine pain. There has never been such a creation of self-forgetting rasa [aesthetic joy] in Bengali literature." [translation by the author]

While celebrating the Bengali new year this Pohela Boishakh, may we remember the melody and the essence of communal harmony embedded in Maimansimha-gitika.

Shamsuddoza Sajen is a journalist and researcher. He can be contacted at [email protected].

World.title: Fizz takes three in Mumbai rout
World.content:
Pace sensation Mustafizur Rahman recorded his best bowling figures of the Indian Premier League today when he finished with 3 for 16 in Sunrisers Hyderabad’s 85-run victory over Mumbai Indians at Vishakhapatnam.

The three-wicket haul took the left-armer to joint-second in the wicket-takers’ list with a total tally of 13 scalps from nine matches. He is one short of Mitchell McClenaghan, who has taken 14 wickets in 10 matches.

The 20-year-old currently has the best bowling average, 15.61, and best economy rate, 6.15, amongs bowlers who have played at least eight matches in the tournament.

The Sunrisers Hyderabad might have depended on Mustafizur a number of times in the ongoing Indian Premier League, but today was a collective effort. Ashish Nehra, Bhuvaneshwar Kumar and Barinder Sran had reduced the Mumbai Indians to 49 for 6 in nine overs before Mustafizur was given the ball.

The wily left-armer sent back Hardik Pandya with his first ball with a cutter which Pandya failed to adjust himself against. Pandya attempted a slice through point, but the ball curled away to the hands of the keeper, with the umpire judging that out even though the television replays were inconclusive.

Then in the very first ball of his second over again, Fizz bowled yet another slower delivery which moved away from the batsman, getting the edge of Tim Southee on the way to the keeper.

The man from Satkhira returned got the scalp of McClenaghan in the final delivery of his third over, getting the batsman to offer a loopy catch to midwicket.

Mustafizur did not get to bowl a fourth over as David Warner gave the other bowlers their chance to mop up the tail. And they did efficiently, bundling out the hosts for just 92 runs in 16.3 overs.

Earlier, brilliant performances from Hyderabad openers, Warner and Shikhar Dhawan helped the team post 177. Dhawan scored 82 off 57 while Warner smacked 48 off 33. Yuvraj Singh also had a good time with the bat, scoring 39 off 23.

World.title: Passengers say 'ghost bookings' now common on crucial V/Line service
World.content:
It is a Friday afternoon and the coach service from Mildura to Swan Hill in Victoria's north-west is fully booked with 38 seats reserved.

But as the bus that links to the Swan Hill-Melbourne train departs, only 18 passengers are on board, leaving 20 empty seats.

These seats are "ghost bookings", for which passengers have not turned up, or have made double bookings.

Mildura station staff and bus drivers said ghost bookings had been common during Victoria's free pubic transport period. They said coach services were often fully booked, but rarely was every seat occupied.

One staff member, who spoke to the ABC on condition of anonymity, told the ABC there had been ghost bookings for nearly every service since public transport became free.

The ABC understands that even when passengers paid $11.40 for a daily V/Line ticket, ghost bookings were already an issue with the service.

With just five V/Line coach services a day leaving Mildura (including two overnight), transport options for those who miss out are limited to a 570-kilometre drive or an expensive, infrequent flight to Melbourne.

Some prospective passengers have taken to arriving at the Mildura V/Line station just prior to the departure of booked-out services in the hope of securing an empty seat.

A sign at Mildura station explaining the 10:05pm coach service to Melbourne is booked out this week. (ABC News: Grace Marshall)

A seat lottery

Mildura resident Karl Smith, who uses the coach service monthly to travel to Melbourne for work and medical appointments, said when he tried to book online, seats were often unavailable.

"I'll try and book online and it says not available and then I'll ring up and they say 'not available'. But usually if you ring five times, they say, 'Oh, something's available,'" he said.

Mr Smith has had to reschedule medical appointments due to pubic transport availability, and has waited up to six months to see specialists.

Even though he had benefited by filling a ghost booked seat, calling it "a plain fluke", he was concerned about future travel plans.

"It's very crappy, unfortunately. But when you think about it, they hold all the cards really," he said.

Karl Smith has had issues with booking the coach, even weeks in advance. (ABC News: Grace Marshall)

Mildura mother Amanda Bernaldo recently faced the same dilemma. She was unable secure her 15-year-old daughter a coach seat from Swan Hill to Mildura.

Ms Bernaldo said she had attempted to book a seat 10 days in advance but the service was already full.

"I wasn't willing to leave my 15-year-old sitting at a bus station on her own in case she could get a seat when someone didn't turn up," she said.

"Ideally, it would have been great if she could have got home on public transport, but that just wasn't the case."

Passengers at Swan Hill also face the same issues with ghost bookings. (ABC News: Grace Marshall)

Ms Bernaldo said the situation had become worse since free transport began.

"I think it's probably come into play a bit over the last four weeks," she said.

"If you can book two seats together for free and not have to sit beside a stranger, most people are going to do that. It's pretty frustrating.

" There would be a lot of people that utilise public transport that can't afford to fly, that are put out by the fact that people are booking seats that they don't intend to use. "

Passengers wait at the Mildura bus station, hoping to get a seat on a 3:55am coach. (ABC News: Grace Marshall)

'We've been at the back of the queue'

Mildura Rural City Council Mayor Ali Cupper said the free public transport initiative highlighted the transport disparity Mildura residents faced.

"We don't have the same baseline of essential public transport infrastructure," she said.

"Every time the government does anything in relation to public transport, particularly in relation to cheap or free travel, it really does highlight that inequity that we face.

"We've got a major regional centre, [in] the most isolated part of the state, which should be at the front of the queue for baseline public transport services to its capital city. But we've been at the back of the queue and it's just bewildering."

Ali Cupper says free public transport highlights a disparity in access between Mildura residents and those in the city. (Supplied: Ali Cupper)

When asked whether it had noticed problems with ghost bookings, or an increase since the free public transport came into affect, V/Line said it was "monitoring demand closely, including on the Mildura to Swan Hill coach route, and adding extra coach support where possible".

"We thank passengers for their understanding when services are busy and will continue to work hard to meet people's travel needs," a spokesperson said.

However, one V/Line staff member, who asked not to be named, was unimpressed with that response.

"Why would you need to add in an additional coach when this one is more than half empty?" they asked.

The Mildura-Swan Hill coach line is one of only two V/Line intrastate services that require seat reservations during the free period.

The other service is the Melbourne-Mansfield route.

World.title: Head-on collision between bus and fuel truck kills 16 people in Indonesia
World.content:
A passenger bus has collided head-on with a fuel tanker truck on a highway on Indonesia's Sumatra island, killing at least 16 people and injuring four others, according to officials.

The intercity bus was travelling on the Trans-Sumatra Highway in North Musi Rawas regency, South Sumatra province, on Wednesday when it struck a tanker truck travelling in the opposite direction, said Mugono, a local disaster management agency official.

The bus carrying at least 20 people was travelling from South Sumatra's Lubuklinggau to Jambi.

"The forceful impact triggered a fire that engulfed both vehicles, leaving many victims trapped inside," said Mugono, who uses a single name like many Indonesians.

The dead include the bus driver and 13 passengers, as well as the tanker's driver and assistant, Mugono said.

Four bus passengers survived the crash and were taken to a nearby health clinic, including three who suffered severe burn injuries and one who sustained minor injuries, Mugono said.

At least 14 killed in train collision near Jakarta The train operator says the crash, on the outskirts of Jakarta, involved a commuter train and a long-distance train.

Mugono said authorities were still determining the total number of fatalities.

Photos and videos released by the National Search and Rescue Agency showed firefighters battling the blaze from the crash while thick plumes of black smoke and orange flames rose into the air.

On the ground were the charred remains of the bus and tanker truck, with twisted metal scattered across the highway.

Rescuers, including disaster officers and traffic police, evacuated victims and cleared the wreckage, though several were pinned inside the vehicles, complicating rescue efforts and disrupting traffic along the highway, Mugono said.

Transport accidents are not uncommon in Indonesia, a vast archipelago nation where buses, trains and even planes are often old and poorly maintained.

Last month, a long-distance train slammed into the back of the women-only carriage of a stationary commuter train near the Bekasi Timur station in West Java, killing 16 women and injuring at least 90 people.

Days later, a train hit a car in Central Java, killing four people including two children.

AP/AFP

World.title: V8 nostalgia has hit F1, and a 'mega engine' could be the future
World.content:
When Mohammed Ben Sulayem, the president of motorsport's governing body the FIA, told media last weekend that Formula 1 was returning to V8 engines, everyone took notice.

It has become the talking point in F1, precisely because it is an idea that seemed implausible just one year ago.

But the much-maligned F1 power units, introduced this season and set to be the engines until the end of 2030, have caused such a stir that Ben Sulayem's V8 declaration felt ironclad.

And Ben Sulayem was not suggesting F1 would completely change its direction; he stated it.

"It's coming. At the end of the day, it's a matter of time," he told media at the Miami Grand Prix.

"In 2031, the V8, the FIA will have the power to do it, without any votes from the PUMs [Power Unit Manufacturers]. That's the regulations. But we want to bring it one year earlier, which everyone now is asking for."

The idea of V8 engines may not evoke much emotion for the millions of fans who have joined the F1 over the past decade.

Formula 1's electrical revolution is losing its spark and V8 power could return As drivers continue to raise objections to Formula 1's new electrical power era, FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has suggested a return to V8 power.

But for those who have been on the ride for a little longer, the idea of F1 returning to the days of screaming V8s almost definitely brought a feeling of nostalgia.

F1 last used V8 engines in 2013, before shifting to the 1.6 litre V6 hybrid engines, which are still used now.

The hybrid era was introduced as a sign of the times. The automotive world was moving towards more electrification and F1 needed to reflect that.

There was a modification to the engine regulations in 2022, but by and large, the engines remained the same for 12 seasons.

But the 2026 model, while technically brilliant, comes with a lot of baggage.

The new power units in F1 cars have not been an immediate hit. (Getty Images: LAT Images/Alastair Staley)

It has almost tripled the amount of electric energy from 120 kilowatts to 350kW, resulting in a near 50-50 split between internal combustion and electric power.

The increased reliance on electrical power means drivers need to spend a lot of their time harvesting energy in the batteries.

This has led to drivers not being able to drive flat-out for longer periods, leading to some speaking against it.

Verstappen says new F1 cars are not fun to drive Four-time Formula 1 world champion Max Verstappen says the 2026 cars are "not so fun", claiming the increasing energy management demands on drivers are "just not Formula 1".

The hybrid power unit is also heavy. It has a minimum weight of 185 kilograms, up 40kg from 2025, and is obese compared to the 2013 V8 engine, which was a minimum of 95kg.

But arguably its biggest issue is the cost, and that is something F1 wants fixed.

"The cost of the power unit is too high, that is definite," F1 chief executive Stefano Domenicali told The Race last month.

"We have the duty to make sure that this business is sustainable. We need to have products that are technologically relevant, and therefore, the cost of this is too high."

There is a cost cap for power unit manufacturers of $US190 million ($265 million), after being allowed to spend $US95 million per year for the past three seasons developing these engines.

This means about $660 million will have been spent by each manufacturer on their power units by the end of this season.

But it is this cost that may be the reason why a return to the old days of the V8 could be a tough sell for manufacturers.

While the FIA has the discretion on the F1 regulations for 2031, having buy-in from manufacturers is important, especially when they would have spent around $660 million by the end of this year on them.

And these new engines, as problematic as they are, have greatly contributed to an increase in manufacturers in the sport.

The 2026 power unit regulations, when written, reflected the automotive industry's push for engines that have more electrification and are simpler.

The regulations not only increased the electrical output but also removed the MGU-H, a complex energy recovery system that recovered exhaust gas and turned it into electricity.

As a result, Audi joined the sport and developed its own engine for the 2026 season, while General Motors is committed to Cadillac being a full works team by the end of the decade.

But no manufacturer has demonstrated the appeal for hybrid power units more than Honda.

Honda is manufacturing power units for Aston Martin. (Getty Images: LAT Images/Andy Hone)

The Japanese automotive giant had exited the sport as a fully fledged manufacturer in 2021, only to make a U-turn on that decision two years later following the release of the 2026 regulations.

The new power units were a major reason for Honda changing its mind because it saw value in investing in the technology to help its business as a whole.

"Our investment in motorsport, especially Formula 1, is a strategic investment to strengthen the long-term competitiveness of Honda's four-wheel business," Shota Yokono, spokesperson for Honda Racing Corporation, told ABC Sport.

"These technologies and skills directly support our future automobile business. Through engineer rotation between motorsport, mass production, and advanced development, we ensure this knowledge is returned to the wider organisation.

"Ultimately, investment in racing is about developing technology, people, and brand — to create future value of Honda."

It is all well and good to declare that F1's future power units will have "very minor electrification", but it still needs to reflect what manufacturers are willing to invest in, even if the push for electric is cooling off.

F1 fans have seen the new era in all its chaotic and thrilling glory Formula 1's new era began with a dramatic, chaotic, and compelling grand prix in Melbourne. While views on the regulations are mixed, fans will likely decide if it is a success or failure.

So, what could be a solution to this problem? It could be having the best of both worlds.

Mercedes has been a major advocate of the current regulations, but when team principal Toto Wolff was asked about the idea of V8s, the Austrian was very interested.

"Long term, I think from a Mercedes standpoint we are open to engine regulations," he said.

"We love V8s. That has only great memories. From our perspective, it's a real Mercedes engine; it revs high.

"And then how do we make it? How do we give enough energy from the battery side to not lose connection to the real world?"

Wolff hypothesised what he called a "mega engine", which could have 800 brake horsepower from the combustion engine, and an extra 400bhp from electric energy.

ABC Sport Daily podcast ABC Sport Daily is your daily sports conversation. We dive into the biggest story of the day and get you up to speed with everything else that's making headlines.

That idea could satisfy those who want an engine that allows F1 drivers to race to the limit, while also ensuring the technology achieved from the billions of dollars invested into this new hybrid era still has value.

"If we swing 100 per cent combustion, then we're looking a bit ridiculous in 2031 or 2030," Wolff said.

"So we need to consider that. Make it simpler and make it a mega engine."

"We recognise the financial realities of [manufacturers] these days … but if it's well-planned and executed, then we, Mercedes, count us in to come back with a real racing engine."

The door appears to be well and truly open for F1 to go back to the future, and the head of the FIA has made clear his intentions.

And Wolff has shown there will be an open mind from those who actually need to build the things.

This debate about what the future power units will look like is going to continue for several years.

But for now, V8 nostalgia is real and its return feels very plausible.

World.title: Jailed preacher refused parole over friendship with terrorists
World.content:
An Australian self-styled Islamic preacher jailed on drug charges has been refused parole because of his extensive correspondence with convicted terrorists while in jail and previous support for Islamic State.

Mohammed Junaid Thorne was jailed for nine years in 2021 after selling tens of thousands of dollars of cocaine and ecstasy to an undercover police officer in a sting orchestrated by counter terrorism police.

The now 36-year-old became eligible for parole in January last year and was at the time refused release on similar grounds.

Thorne was one of three people arrested in Sydney after NSW counter terrorism detectives uncovered an illicit drug and firearm supply network. (Supplied: NSW Police)

Thorne can apply every 12 months for his parole to be reviewed and this is the second time he has been refused.

On April 27, the New South Wales parole board again ordered he not be released, because it could not be satisfied Thorne would "not engage in, or incite or assist others to engage in terrorist acts of violent extremism".

Online posts about Islamic State investigated

Thorne has long been the focus of authorities after declaring himself a "sheikh" — a Muslim religious authority or leader, and recording lengthy sermons on his interpretation of Islam.

At least one sermon recorded on video was delivered in front of a symbol on a black flag commonly associated with Islamic State (IS).

He has previously denied supporting violent extremism or being linked to any terrorist groups including IS.

Thorne once delivered a sermon in front of a symbol adopted by Islamic State, which reads "Muhammad is the Messenger of God".

Born in Perth, Australia, Thorne was taken to Saudi Arabia by his stepfather and mother at the age of 10, telling an assessing psychologist he received a "strict" Muslim upbringing there.

Thorne was deported by Saudi authorities in 2013 after protesting that country's jailing of his older brother, Shayden Thorne, for four years on terrorism charges.

Shayden went on to become one of the so-called "tinny terrorists" for his involvement in a bold but ultimately doomed plan in which six Australian men planned to sail from northern Queensland to the southern Philippines to help religious militants overthrow the government and impose Sharia law.

After arriving back in Perth, Mohammed Junaid Thorne styled himself as a "sheikh" — a Muslim religious scholar or leader — preaching under the banner of "Millatu Ibrahim", which shares the name and logo of a proscribed terrorist group once banned in Germany whose founders went on to die fighting for Islamic State in Syria and Iraq.

In 2014 the federal government confirmed it was investigating online posts purporting to be linked to Thorne that praised the fall of Mosul in Iraq to "our brothers in the Islamic State of Iraq and Sham (ISIS)".

According to Amnesty International, Islamic State fighters attempting to establish an Islamic caliphate in Iraq during this period committed crimes against humanity which included torture and the rape and sexual enslavement of Iraqi women and girls taken captive during the conflict.

The Australian government had become concerned that Australians were being radicalised by IS sympathisers and travelling overseas to fight in the conflict.

In 2015, Thorne was jailed for nine months for travelling on a false name.

Junaid Thorne was charged for travelling under a false name, which he said was a bid to avoid scrutiny of his movements by authorities. (ABC News: Ben Worsley)

After this period of incarceration he is believed to have relocated from Perth to Sydney where the drug offences occurred.

In assessing his application for parole, the NSW parole board considered a report by violent extremism expert Dr Joshua Roose which found Thorne had previously expressed support for IS ideology, which included giving a lecture in front of a banner depicting an Islamic State flag and posting public messages on social media supporting IS leaders.

Dr Roose said prior to being jailed, Thorne had been linked to individuals who had advocated, supported or engaged in acts of terrorism of violent extremism.

Thorne was also linked to the now shuttered Al Furqan Centre in Melbourne, which Dr Roose said promoted violent jihad.

Dr Roose said Thorne had also posted publicly supporting slain radical Abdul Numan Haider, who was also linked to the Al Furqan centre before being shot dead after stabbing two counter-terrorism officers outside a Melbourne police station.

Exchanges with violent extremists scuppers parole bid

The board was also provided 800 pages of correspondence between Thorne and 10 other inmates who had all been convicted of terrorism-related offending.

One of them was Talal Alameddine, who is jailed for supplying the gun to 15-year-old Farhad Mohammad who shot dead NSW police employee Curtis Cheng in a 2017 terrorist attack outside a suburban police station in western Sydney.

Accountant Curtis Cheng (far left), pictured here with his family, was murdered in a terrorist attack targeting Parramatta police station. (Supplied: NSW Police)

Thorne also corresponded with Mohammad Kiad and Omar Al-Kutobi who are serving 20-year terms for planning a stabbing terrorist attack in February 2015, after recording homemade videos in front of IS flags and acquiring a hunting knife and machete.

Thorne was also in contact with radicalised Sydney man Isaac El Matari who was jailed in part over his "grandiose" plans to head up an IS Australia chapter and mount an IS insurgency in Australia.

Another of his correspondents was Bourhan Hraichie, jailed for planning an Islamic State-inspired police shooting and who carved an IS-inspired mark into his cellmate's forehead.

NSW prosecutors conceded that none of the 800 pages of correspondence expressly supported acts of terrorism, but said it remained significant due to Thorne's previously expressed support for IS — claims Thorne had denied in the past.

"The correspondence continued to reflect a strong adherence to Salafist ideology to which, in Dr Roose's opinion, the offender had previously expressed an adherence and from which he had obviously never resiled," the parole board's report found.

A Countering Violent Extremism (CVE) report found Thorne had not since his imprisonment "demonstrated any change in his views" and that other inmates appeared to "continue to view the offender as "a source of religious authority".

It did note Thorne had since July 2023 consistently engaged positively in a de-radicalisation program, known as "PRISM" that aims to build "resilience to radicalisation through diversion, disengagement, and desistance".

Thorne complained to WA Police in 2014 about receiving death threats, following reports of his support for Haider. (ABC News: Rebecca Trigger)

Thorne's lawyer suggested that this engagement, along with the view from a psychologist that Thorne did not hold or promote extremist ideology, supported his release.

However the state submitted that engagement was happening at the same time Thorne was corresponding with those convicted of terror offences.

The state also submitted that between February and April last year, after his last parole application was refused, Thorne had made several "unapproved" calls in which he "made statements which were unequivocally to the effect that his extremists beliefs had not changed" which contradicted statements made by Thorne in the deradicalisation program.

"Taken in isolation, the summary prepared in November 2025 might support the proposition that the offender … had disengaged from his extremist views," the parole board's report noted.

"However, counsel emphasised the need to assess the issues on the whole of the evidence."

Thorne's sentence will expire on July, 30 2028. He can reapply for parole next year.

World.title: Fowler's Manchester City wins WSL title ahead of Matildas teammates
World.content:
Mary Fowler has become a Women's Super League champion with Manchester City, but some of her Matildas teammates have been left frustrated in their bid to lift the English title with Arsenal.

Fowler and her City colleagues were gifted the crown on Wednesday night, local time, even though they were not in action.

Instead, they watched it together on TV as Arsenal, featuring Caitlin Foord in their ranks, failed to win at Brighton & Hove Albion, the 1-1 draw being enough to send the trophy to City for the first time in a decade and to spark huge celebrations among the squad.

City could thank Brighton's Australian manager Dario Vidosic, who helped orchestrate another shock with his well-drilled party poopers.

Arsenal, 11 points behind at the start of the night but with three games in hand, could only stay in the race by winning convincingly to eat into the goal difference between the two sides, but they knew even this might not be enough.

Still looking flat after their weekend's Champions League exit to Lyonnes, they always had their work cut out once Fuka Tsunoda struck just before half-time for Brighton.

Frida Maanum's 62nd-minute strike levelled proceedings but, when the visitors could not conjure up a winner at Broadfield Stadium, Andree Jeglertz was able to celebrate silverware in his first season in charge at City.

ABC Sport Daily podcast ABC Sport Daily is your daily sports conversation. We dive into the biggest story of the day and get you up to speed with everything else that's making headlines.

It sealed a triumphant comeback for Australia midfielder Fowler, who has been at City for four years and become a hugely popular player there.

The 23-year-old only returned to action in February after being out for over nine months with an ACL injury suffered in the Women's FA Cup semifinal in April 2025.

"Helping guide this team to the WSL title is something I will never forget," coach Jeglertz said.

"The girls have met every challenge in front of them head-on and have been an absolute joy to coach this season."

Two of Arsenal's Matildas did not play, with Steph Catley still nursing an injury and Kyra Cooney-Cross's season already over to allow her to jet back home to Australia to be with her poorly mother, so it was down to Foord to fire the Gunners' challenge.

But she was denied by a fingertip save from Nigerian goalie Chiamaka Nnadozie in the second half as Arsenal failed to gain the three points needed on the night that Sam Kerr's Chelsea finally saw their run of six consecutive championships ended.

AAP

World.title: Victorians wake to snow month out from ski season
World.content:
Victorians have woken to snow this morning as a cold blast brings below-zero temperatures to the state's alpine peaks.

At Mt Baw Baw in the state's east, 15 centimetres of snow fell overnight, turning the village white.

"It looks like an amazing, beautiful white wonderland," resort spokeswoman Sally Brook said.

The early snowfall has given hope to resort managers just a month out from the ski season opening on the June long weekend.

"The ground getting cold is exactly what we needed leading into the King's birthday," Ms Brook said.

"The weather was sort of looking warm, and we all start to get a bit edgy, but this weather is exactly what we need."

Ms Brook said anyone planning to visit Mt Baw Baw today would need to fit chains on their wheels due to the icy conditions.

"The road is quite treacherous at the moment, so please, please get some chains if you're coming up."

Motorists are being advised to take extra care on icy roads this morning. (Supplied)

Bureau of Meteorology forecaster Kate Doyle said today's cold weather meant that snow had fallen "down to some pretty impressive locations".

"Particularly on the snow cam at Mount Buller, there's quite a lot of snow at the village square there," Ms Doyle said.

"Certainly, a cold change has made its way through. We are expecting a bit of follow-up, particularly wind through the region, as we continue to see that [cold front] making its way through the next few days."

Snow has fallen at Wulgulmerang in East Gippsland this morning. (Supplied)

At Wulgulmerang, in the state's far east, cattle farmer Gordon Moon told ABC Gippsland snow was stuck to the top of the trees when he woke up this morning.

Mr Moon said snow was not unusual in the area, which is more than 1,050 metres above sea level.

"You come up through Buchan, W Tree, Gelantipy, and Wulgulmerang is at the top of the hill before you drop down going towards Jindabyne," he said.

"I've seen snow nearly every month of the year here, and my mother has seen it every month of the year up here."

World.title: Commercial fisher raises $25k to fight demersal fishing ban in WA
World.content:
A commercial fishing business in Western Australia's South West has crowdfunded more than $25,000 to fund legal action against the government's ban on demersal fishing.

It has been more than four months since the state government brought in restrictions permanently banning commercial demersal fishing along 900 kilometres of the West Coast bioregion, from Kalbarri to Augusta.

Fisheries Minister Jackie Jarvis has defended the move, which the state government says is aimed at rebuilding demersal fish stocks on the verge of extinction.

The move has sparked widespread backlash and protests, including shark heads being dumped at the minister's office.

Legal advice sought

Since launching an online fundraiser at the weekend, Southwestern Fisheries in Bunbury has raised more than $25,000 in donations, with a goal of $35,000.

Commercial fisherman and seafood retailer Brian Scimone is planning to fight the fishing ban. (ABC South West WA: Gabrielle Becerra Mellet)

Seafood companies in WA's north also launched legal action in the Supreme Court to challenge the decision last year.

Brian Scimone said his family business would put the funds in a trust and use the money for legal advice on challenging the demersal ban and accompanying buyback scheme.

"We're not seeing any progress," he said.

"We're not getting any further advanced on whether we can reopen the fishery and the compensation is nowhere near enough for a lifetime of loss.

"This is a life ban."

Wide-reaching impacts

Impacts have been felt across the marine industry since the decision was announced late last year.

Nathan Boyce owns a business in Bunbury servicing commercial vessels between Broome and Augusta.

He said the day after the demersal ban was announced, he lost a $150,000 motor engine sale.

Nathan Boyce says his marine business had taken a hit from the ban. (ABC South West WA: Gabrielle Becerra Mellet)

"Once a commercial fisherman doesn't have a business, he's not going to spend any money with me," Mr Boyce said.

"[Business with commercial fishermen] has just dropped right off."

Buyback scheme 'too low'

People in the West Coast bioregion affected by the ban have been given six weeks to apply under the government's $20 million buyback of commercial licences.

The compulsory buyout determines amounts paid based on market value, with methodology in line with industry feedback, according to the government.

The state government implemented the ban along the entire West Coast bioregion. (ABC News: Bridget McArthur)

Mr Scimone said he had opted not to apply for the scheme.

"It doesn't even enter the millions and we're one of the biggest holders on the coast," he said.

"The compensation offered is not good enough.

"We have boats that are purpose-built, equipment that's purpose-built, factories deemed unusable, nets and fishing gear deemed unusable."

'Difficult decisions'

In response to prospective legal action, a state government spokesperson said demersal fish species such as dhufish and snapper were on the verge of extinction in parts of WA.

"The state government would like to thank all recreational and commercial fishers who are playing their part to help protect our demersal species," the spokesperson said.

"While these have been difficult decisions to make, they had to be made.

"Urgent action is needed to save them for the future generations of fishers."

World.title: PSG see off Bayern in gripping Champions League semi to set Arsenal date
World.content:
Holders Paris St Germain secured a 1-1 draw at Bayern Munich to reach the Champions League final, earning a 6-5 aggregate victory after a compelling second leg that was far cagier than their goal-laden first encounter.

The French side will face Arsenal in the May 30 showcase game in Budapest after the London club's 1-0 victory over Atletico Madrid on Wednesday morning (AEST) secured a 2-1 aggregate win.

Bayern, hoping to reach their first Champions League final since 2020, saw their treble hopes dashed and can now only add the German Cup to their Bundesliga crown this season.

Holding a 5-4 advantage from a scintillating first leg, PSG got off to a perfect start when Ousmane Dembele, who scored twice last week, rifled home from a perfectly timed Khvicha Kvaratskhelia cutback in the third minute. Dembele and Kvaratskhelia had both scored twice in the first leg.

Bayern upped the pressure almost instantly and went close but both Michael Olise and Luis Diaz narrowly missed the target with shots from the edge of the box.

The Germans had boxed their opponents in their own half but keeper Manuel Neuer still had to come to their rescue in the 33rd minute, palming Joao Neves' header wide to keep Bayern in the game.

ABC Sport Daily podcast ABC Sport Daily is your daily sports conversation. We dive into the biggest story of the day and get you up to speed with everything else that's making headlines.

His PSG counterpart Matvei Safonov responded with a superb save of his own, stopping Jamal Musiala's low drive from close range a minute before the break.

It was initially one-way traffic after the interval with PSG again sitting back, but threatening on the counter-attack.

With the hosts, who needed two goals, growing more desperate, PSG found more space in the second half and went close through Desire Doue and Kvaratskhelia late in the game.

Bayern's top scorer Kane, who had hardly had a look-in, found just enough space to drill in a stoppage-time equaliser, scoring for a seventh consecutive game in the competition.

But his 55th goal across all competitions this season for Bayern came too late as the hosts ran out of time.

Reuters

World.title: Antisemitism royal commission LIVE: Witnesses begin evidence on day four of hearing
World.content:
Good morning, and welcome to our live coverage of the Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion.

It’s day four of the first block of hearings, which is focusing on defining antisemitism, lived experiences of antisemitism and the impact on Jewish Australians, and how to assess the prevalence of antisemitism in institutions.

Yesterday we heard from more than a dozen witnesses, many of whom appeared anonymously, to share their experiences of antisemitism in schools and community groups.

Parents spoke about their children being confronted with Nazi salutes and racist slurs, and a teacher from Tasmania described the growth of “casual” antisemitism in schools since the October 7 attack by Hamas.

Outside the Sydney hearing venue a man wearing a T-shirt with a swastika was moved on by police, and later charged with behaving in an offensive manner in a public place and displaying a prohibited Nazi symbol in a public place. He will appear before Manly Local Court on May 27.

World.title: Watch live: investors take aim at Kyle & Jackie O’s former bosses
World.content:
Breaking BusinessCompaniesMedia & marketing Watch live: investors take aim at Kyle & Jackie O’s former bosses Calum Jaspan Updated May 7, 2026 — 9:39am ,first published 8:46am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

The chair of Kyle Sandilands and Jackie ‘O’ Henderson’s former radio network has vowed to keep fighting their $170 million combined lawsuits, telling shareholders at the company’s annual meeting that he was personally investing $500,000 into ARN in a show of confidence. Chief executive Michael Stephenson told the meeting that ARN had lost $26 million last year in advertising revenue from clients pulling spending over “brand safety” concerns, in a reference to the crude and sexualised content on The Kyle & Jackie O Show. Loading “Over time, I expect that a significant percentage of the $26 million of revenue that was lost through the year because of brand safety concerns to return,” Stephenson said. Two months after sacking the hosts of The Kyle and Jackie O Show, KIIS network owner ARN Media’s chief executive, chairman and board are facing fired-up investors and the media for the first time at the company’s annual general meeting in North Sydney.



Proxy votes showed company chair Hamish McLennan would be re-elected as chair, despite 20 per cent of proxy votes opposing his re-election. In the lead-up to the meeting, McLennan faced investor calls to step down after handing Kyle Sandilands and Jackie “O” Henderson their $200 million in combined contracts and presiding over an 87 per cent decline in the valuation of ARN. ARN chief executive Michael Stephenson (left) and chair Hamish McLennan at the ARN media annual general meeting. Dominic Lorrimer The company has faced heavy media scrutiny – and duelling legal cases – after handing Sandilands and Henderson the most expensive talent deals in Australian media history, and then tearing them up after a little more than a year. “If I was Hamish, I’d see the writing on the wall,” one key shareholder told this masthead last month, noting a suite of poor strategic decisions including the $307 million purchase of regional broadcaster Grant Broadcasters just five years ago, a figure that dwarves the entire company’s current valuation several times over. At the meeting, veteran investor David Kingston asked McLennan a string of hostile questions, including asking him to recount the “the three biggest mistakes you and the board have made that have contributed to the massive shareholder loss?”



McLennan called the question “loaded” and said the entire traditional media sector was under pressure. McLennan said the company regularly reflected on its performance, but that he was committed to ARN. “We’re not happy with where we’re at the moment,” McLennan said. “I think hindsight is a wonderful thing when you look at a range of different decisions, but it’s a very, very fluid environment, and I think the board stands by all the decisions they make.” He defended the Grant acquisition, saying it was contributing to earnings. “It’s been a fantastic acquisition for us,” McLennan said, after Kingston said he was “shocked” by his defence of the purchase. McLennan, who has faced some scrutiny over his relatively small shareholding in the company despite being its chair, told investors at the AGM he will invest $500,000 into ARN. “I will be making this investment in my personal capacity as a demonstration of my confidence in the company’s strategy,” he said. Two days ago, this masthead reported McLennan is selling his Sydney home for $36 million.



During his address, McLennan reinforced ARN’s position that Henderson has told the company she could no longer work with Sandilands and therefore backed out of her contract to deliver The Kyle & Jackie O Show. Related Article Radio The ‘besties’ behind the Kyle and Jackie O reckoning He said she had told ARN: “direct contact with Mr Sandilands [was] now untenable.” McLennan said that ARN was confident in its litigation strategy. “I would like to assure shareholders that the board is committed to defending these claims and actively pursuing the cross-claims,” he said. While two key proxy advisory firms backed McLennan’s reelection, one, CGI Glass Lewis, argued Stephenson’s fixed $1.1 million contract is too much, based on the fact it is well above the median $812,000 paid to ASX250-300 companies, and ARN is not even on that list.



Hamish McLennan, chairman of ARN Media, which owns KIIS FM. Dominic Lorrimer Related Article Exclusive

Radio How KIIS cashed in on Kyle & Jackie O’s ‘explosive fights’ “This approach is notable in the context of the Company’s declining market capitalisation, which reduced from approximately $578 million at end of FY2021, to around $300 million over the following two years, and further to $124 million at FY2025 year-end and approximately $74 million as at 17 April 2026,” the report said. ARN has defended Stephenson’s pay packet based on his responsibilities and talent. The AGM is the first for Michael Stephenson, who initially joined ARN as its chief operating officer. He was previously chief sales officer at Nine (the owner of this masthead) for a decade.



This week, Sandilands and Henderson filed their defences in countersuits lodged against the duo by ARN. Sandilands’ legal team allege KIIS FM and ARN cashed in on he and Henderson’s on-air feuds, even going to lengths to promote them, a feature of the show’s daily soap opera drama. “[ARN] publicly exploited and thereby sought to monetise the conduct,” Sandilands’ lawyers said in the documents. “[They did this] without directing or requesting Mr Sandilands or Ms Henderson, not to engage in conduct of that kind.” The Business Briefing newsletter delivers major stories, exclusive coverage and expert opinion. Sign up to get it every weekday morning.

World.title: WA news LIVE: First Home Buyer exemptions increased as Perth property prices soar
World.content:
With Perth property price growth leading the nation and the median house price now more than $1 million, the state government has lifted the first home buyer stamp duty exemption from $700,000 to properties valued at $800,000 or less.

The changes were announced today, just hours before Premier Roger Cook prepares to hand down the 2026/27 State Budget.

It is the third time the state government has increased the stamp duty exemption cut off, with this most recent time increasing it by $100,000.

The changes, worth $297 million, are expected to deliver savings of up to $22,515 to people buying a new or established home, and up to $25,390 when building a home.

Those who buy or build a home for $600,000 or less will pay no stamp duty, while stamp duty concessions will be available for homes up to $800,000.

The $10,000 First Homes Owners Grant cap will also increase from $750,000 to $800,000.

World.title: Australian who left hantavirus-hit cruise ship after first death has ‘returned home’: report
World.content:
Breaking NationalIllness Australian who left hantavirus-hit cruise ship after first death has ‘returned home’: report Jack Gramenz May 7, 2026 — 9:29am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

A passenger who was aboard the cruise ship hit by an outbreak of hantavirus has returned to Australia, according to a passenger still on board the stricken vessel. The Australian was among 23 people who left the ship at St Helena on April 21, one of whom has since tested positive to the virus and is now in hospital in Switzerland, the passenger said. Loading The incubation period for the virus can last several weeks. Those who remain on board are isolating under strict hygiene measures. The passenger from Spain told Spanish newspaper El Pais the group left the ship on the island of Saint Helena 10 days after the first death on board the ship was recorded.



“Until three days ago, no one had contacted them,” the Spanish passenger was quoted as saying. “The Australian went back to Australia, the one from Taiwan to Taiwan, the Americans to all corners of North America. The Englishman to England, the Dutch to their homes,” they said. One of the departed passengers, who reportedly “wasn’t feeling well” when they departed, went to hospital in Switzerland and has since tested positive to the virus. Another person linked to the ship is in intensive care at a hospital in South Africa. Three deaths have been linked to the outbreak, with eight total cases recorded.



On Wednesday, specialist teams transferred three people from the ship. The ship is currently off the west coast of Africa, destined for the Canary Islands, but the regional government in the Spanish territory is opposed to the ship docking. Health workers in protective gear evacuate patients from the MV Hondius cruise ship into an ambulance at a port in Praia, Cape Verde on Wednesday. AP “This decision [by the Spanish government to allow the docking] is not based on any technical criteria, nor is there sufficient information to reassure the public or guarantee their safety,” Canary Islands President Fernando Clavijo told Madrid radio station, COPE.



The luxury cruise ship has been marooned for days off the coast of Cape Verde. “Oceanwide Expeditions remains in close and continual discussion with relevant authorities regarding our exact point of arrival, quarantine and screening procedures for all guests, and a precise timeline,” the operator said in a statement. “We are unable to confirm the details of onward travel for guests at this stage.” The hantavirus-hit MV Hondius is destined for the Canary Islands. AP Four Australians were on board the ship, though their identities have not been disclosed. In a statement, DFAT told Reuters it was aware that Australians were on the ship but was not aware of any being affected by the reported hantavirus outbreak.



DFAT has been contacted regarding the Spanish newspaper’s report of an Australian disembarking the ship in Saint Helena and returning home. Health authorities say about 150 people from 23 countries are on board the ship. Passengers, some of whom have been aboard since March 20, have reported moods swinging between fear and boredom: empty lounges, quiet decks, hot drinks, face masks, medical checks, and the uncertainty of not knowing when and how their journey will end. with Reuters

World.title: ‘Time to say goodbye’: Possible Epstein suicide note released
World.content:
Breaking WorldNorth AmericaEpstein fallout ‘Time to say goodbye’: Possible Epstein suicide note released Benjamin Weiser , Jan Ransom and Steve Eder May 7, 2026 — 9:20am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

A federal judge has released a suicide note purportedly written by Jeffrey Epstein that was sealed for years as part of the criminal case of his cellmate. “They investigated me for months — FOUND NOTHING!!!” the note begins, adding that the result were charges going back many years. A federal judge has released a suicide note purportedly written by Jeffrey Epstein that was sealed for years as part of the criminal case of his cellmate. Southern District of New York “It is a treat to be able to choose one’s time to say goodbye,” the note continued. “Watcha want me to do — Bust out cryin!!” the note reads.



“NO FUN,” it concludes, with those words underlined. “NOT WORTH IT!!” Epstein’s cellmate, Nicholas Tartaglione, said he discovered the note in July 2019 after Epstein was found unresponsive with a strip of cloth wrapped around his neck. Epstein survived that incident, but he was found dead weeks later at age 66 in the now shuttered Metropolitan Correctional Centre in lower Manhattan. Related Article Epstein fallout Epstein’s possible suicide note hidden from public view The note was made public on Wednesday by Judge Kenneth M. Karas of U.S. District Court in White Plains, New York, who oversaw the cellmate’s case. The judge acted after The New York Times petitioned the court last week to unseal the document and published an article in which Tartaglione described the note and how it came into his possession. The Times has not authenticated the note, which was placed on the court docket Wednesday evening (US time).



The document remained hidden from public view even as the Justice Department released millions of pages of documents related to Epstein in a move of unprecedented transparency. The Times searched those records and did not find a copy of the note. (A spokesperson from the Justice Department said the agency had never seen it.) The search did turn up a cryptic two-page chronology that described how the note became caught up in Tartaglione’s complicated legal case. The chronology said that Tartaglione’s lawyers authenticated the note, though it did not explain how. Jeffrey Epstein. Alamy Stock Photo Tartaglione, a former police officer in Briarcliff Manor, New York, shared a cell with Epstein while awaiting trial in a quadruple murder case. He told the Times in recent phone interviews from a California prison that he found the note in a graphic novel after Epstein was taken out of their cell after the apparent suicide attempt. “I opened the book to read and there it was,” Tartaglione said. It was written on a piece of yellow paper ripped from a legal pad, he said.



Nicholas Tartaglione, Epstein’s former cellmate. NYT The New York City medical examiner ruled Epstein’s death a suicide. In the years since, revelations of security lapses inside the jail have spawned endless theories about how Epstein died and whether he was murdered. When jail officials asked Epstein about red marks on his neck after the incident in July, he first said that Tartaglione had attacked him and that he was not suicidal. Tartaglione has long denied assaulting Epstein, who later told jail officials he “never had any issues” with his cellmate. Tartaglione said he gave the note to his lawyers because he believed it could have been helpful if Epstein continued to claim that he had tried to hurt him. Tartaglione was convicted in 2023 and is now serving four life sentences. He has maintained his innocence and has appealed his conviction. The note apparently became part of a drawn-out legal dispute among Tartaglione’s lawyers. Documents related to the conflict were placed under a court seal to protect attorney-client privilege, the filings say.



Before unsealing the note, Karas asked the parties in the case to provide their views on The Times′ request that the materials be made public. The US attorney’s office in Manhattan, which prosecuted Tartaglione, did not contest the note’s release. In a letter to the judge, the prosecutors wrote that “there appears to be a strong public interest in the circumstances surrounding Epstein’s death”. This article originally appeared in The New York Times. Get a note directly from our foreign correspondents on what’s making headlines around the world.

World.title: Cousin! The Bear’s surprise episode will leave you desperate for season five
World.content:
Spoilers CultureTV & radioStreaming Cousin! The Bear’s surprise episode will leave you desperate for season five Meg Watson May 7, 2026 — 8:59am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

The Bear has served up a new standalone episode ahead of its fifth – and final – season next month. And just like the past two seasons of this award-winning show, it’s likely to divide viewers. If you’d like to go in completely blind, the one-hour instalment is available to watch now on Disney+ under the title Gary (it’s not listed with the other episodes of The Bear). Otherwise, read on to get a sense of what to expect and what this means for the upcoming season of the show. No spoilers until the final section, I promise! Jon Bernthal as Michael Berzatto, Ebon Moss-Bachrach as Richard “Richie” Jerimovich in a surprise standalone episode of The Bear. FX/Disney+ What’s it about? As you might suspect given the inclusion of Jon Bernthal’s character Mikey, whose death by suicide triggers the events of the first season, Gary is a prequel to the events of The Bear. The episode is essentially a mini road movie, following a trip Mikey and Richie (Ebon Moss-Bachrach) took shortly before the birth of Richie’s daughter to Gary, Indiana.

World.title: Paterson’s video stunt the Coalition’s One Nation crisis writ small
World.content:
Analysis PoliticsFederalByelection Paterson’s video stunt the Coalition’s One Nation crisis writ small Natassia Chrysanthos May 7, 2026 — 8:49am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Australians can trust that spats outside polling booths and fights over political posters will signal when election day is around the corner. Usually, these disputes involve volunteers. Sometimes local candidates. They don’t usually implicate senior politicians (although it has happened before). Wednesday’s addition to the genre was a rare example of the latter, as Liberal Senator James Paterson – one of Angus Taylor’s senior shadow ministers and a party powerbroker – filmed his clash with a One Nation volunteer outside a booth in Albury just days before the Farrer byelection. Loading Unlike most viral moments that emerge from the silliness and thick emotion of pre-poll booths, this three-minute snippet was telling of the dynamics at play ahead of polling day.



The substance of the two men’s disagreement, according to the video footage, was whether it mattered that One Nation candidate David Farley previously tried to stand for Labor. Related Article Byelection ‘That’s assault’: One Nation volunteer grabs Liberal senator’s phone in clash outside polling booth It is unclear how the interaction began, but Paterson filmed their verbal sparring for two minutes, including some colourful name-calling from the One Nation volunteer. The man, who seemed unaware he was being recorded, turned away from the conversation at several points. When he eventually realised Paterson’s phone was filming, he was affronted and grabbed the device. Paterson claimed assault. Paterson was right to say that voters deserve to know the political history of the aspiring One Nation candidate. The man was wrong to grab his phone. Both Farley and Pauline Hanson condemned the incident. Was it the right move for Paterson to keep engaging in the argument and film it, however, rather than walk away? It’s unlikely this viral moment will do the Liberals many favours in Farrer – particularly when the characters in this contest have already been cast as disgruntled country folk who are fighting back against a political establishment in the cities that has ignored them.



This framing is only reinforced by the optics of Paterson (a pedigree politician from Melbourne who came through a think-tank before landing in parliament) having a spat with a local volunteer over the specifics of defamation law. Hanson’s chief-of-staff James Ashby jumped on that view, despite his boss’ apology. Claiming Paterson “went looking for a blue”, he told Sky News: “You’ve got a bloke who’s on $300,000 a year deliberately going out there, rage baiting a pensioner who God only knows what he’s having to live off.” The evidence is already sitting in Farley’s social media comments. Underneath the candidate’s Facebook post condemning the incident – which contains the raw footage – there are hundreds complaining that the volunteer was goaded into the altercation. It also shows how difficult it has been for the Coalition to land the right attack lines against One Nation. There is a tension in keeping would-be Liberals and Nationals voters onside without disparaging or condescending them, while laying blows powerful enough to make a dent on the party’s surging popularity. Voters jumping the fence from the Coalition to One Nation don’t paint all Liberal and National MPs with the same brush, but they do want to send a message. Indeed, the One Nation volunteer praised Paterson and Liberal frontbencher Andrew Hastie as two of the good ones, before the interaction soured. It is, evidently, a delicate relationship to be managed.



Taylor’s tactic has been to call prospective One Nation voters his friends and avoid going too hard, while Nationals leader Matt Canavan is more forthright. Paterson has been one of the Liberals’ most strident critics of the rival party, leading the charge against Hanson’s hiring of convicted sex offender Sean Black, whom she was then forced to sack. He’s done more than most colleagues to portray One Nation as incompetent and unserious. Related Article Byelection A protest vote is brewing in Sussan Ley’s seat – but it won’t be simple Yet these messages are again muddled by the Liberals’ and Nationals’ decision to preference One Nation above Farley’s main contender, independent Michelle Milthorpe, on Saturday – a move that could hand Hanson’s party the seat. Finally, it is telling that Farley’s Labor ties have become such a lightning rod in this byelection. Not because they’re unworthy of scrutiny, but because they seem to be the best blow the Coalition can land – hence the corflutes photoshopping Farley in Labor red that spurred Wednesday’s conflict. It’s a smart move from the Coalition to seize on voters’ deep scepticism of Labor. But the reality is also that the Coalition has little else to sell voters who feel their living standards have declined despite electing either the Nationals or Liberals in every vote since the seat was created.



While contempt for Labor runs through the electorate, many now hold the same feelings for the Liberals and Nationals who have spent much of the last year infighting, and before that were in government for years delivering controversial water policies or insufficient improvements to regional services. And so the One Nation volunteer’s response to Paterson’s argument about Farley – that painting him in Labor red is just a desperate attempt to distract from how scared the Liberals and Nationals are of Saturday’s result – might well indicate how thousands of other voters are thinking. The Coalition will keep trying to persuade them otherwise, but as Paterson can now attest, it won’t be easy. Cut through the noise of federal politics with news, views and expert analysis. World.title: Antisemitism royal commission LIVE: Witnesses begin evidence on day four of hearing
World.content:
Good morning, and welcome to our live coverage of the Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion.

It’s day four of the first block of hearings, which is focusing on defining antisemitism, lived experiences of antisemitism and the impact on Jewish Australians, and how to assess the prevalence of antisemitism in institutions.

Yesterday we heard from more than a dozen witnesses, many of whom appeared anonymously, to share their experiences of antisemitism in schools and community groups.

Parents spoke about their children being confronted with Nazi salutes and racist slurs, and a teacher from Tasmania described the growth of “casual” antisemitism in schools since the October 7 attack by Hamas.

Outside the Sydney hearing venue a man wearing a T-shirt with a swastika was moved on by police, and later charged with behaving in an offensive manner in a public place and displaying a prohibited Nazi symbol in a public place. He will appear before Manly Local Court on May 27.

World.title: Watch live: investors take aim at Kyle & Jackie O’s former bosses
World.content:
Breaking BusinessCompaniesMedia & marketing Watch live: investors take aim at Kyle & Jackie O’s former bosses Calum Jaspan Updated May 7, 2026 — 9:39am ,first published 8:46am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

The chair of Kyle Sandilands and Jackie ‘O’ Henderson’s former radio network has vowed to keep fighting their $170 million combined lawsuits, telling shareholders at the company’s annual meeting that he was personally investing $500,000 into ARN in a show of confidence. Chief executive Michael Stephenson told the meeting that ARN had lost $26 million last year in advertising revenue from clients pulling spending over “brand safety” concerns, in a reference to the crude and sexualised content on The Kyle & Jackie O Show. Loading “Over time, I expect that a significant percentage of the $26 million of revenue that was lost through the year because of brand safety concerns to return,” Stephenson said. Two months after sacking the hosts of The Kyle and Jackie O Show, KIIS network owner ARN Media’s chief executive, chairman and board are facing fired-up investors and the media for the first time at the company’s annual general meeting in North Sydney.



Proxy votes showed company chair Hamish McLennan would be re-elected as chair, despite 20 per cent of proxy votes opposing his re-election. In the lead-up to the meeting, McLennan faced investor calls to step down after handing Kyle Sandilands and Jackie “O” Henderson their $200 million in combined contracts and presiding over an 87 per cent decline in the valuation of ARN. ARN chief executive Michael Stephenson (left) and chair Hamish McLennan at the ARN media annual general meeting. Dominic Lorrimer The company has faced heavy media scrutiny – and duelling legal cases – after handing Sandilands and Henderson the most expensive talent deals in Australian media history, and then tearing them up after a little more than a year. “If I was Hamish, I’d see the writing on the wall,” one key shareholder told this masthead last month, noting a suite of poor strategic decisions including the $307 million purchase of regional broadcaster Grant Broadcasters just five years ago, a figure that dwarves the entire company’s current valuation several times over. At the meeting, veteran investor David Kingston asked McLennan a string of hostile questions, including asking him to recount the “the three biggest mistakes you and the board have made that have contributed to the massive shareholder loss?”



McLennan called the question “loaded” and said the entire traditional media sector was under pressure. McLennan said the company regularly reflected on its performance, but that he was committed to ARN. “We’re not happy with where we’re at the moment,” McLennan said. “I think hindsight is a wonderful thing when you look at a range of different decisions, but it’s a very, very fluid environment, and I think the board stands by all the decisions they make.” He defended the Grant acquisition, saying it was contributing to earnings. “It’s been a fantastic acquisition for us,” McLennan said, after Kingston said he was “shocked” by his defence of the purchase. McLennan, who has faced some scrutiny over his relatively small shareholding in the company despite being its chair, told investors at the AGM he will invest $500,000 into ARN. “I will be making this investment in my personal capacity as a demonstration of my confidence in the company’s strategy,” he said. Two days ago, this masthead reported McLennan is selling his Sydney home for $36 million.



During his address, McLennan reinforced ARN’s position that Henderson has told the company she could no longer work with Sandilands and therefore backed out of her contract to deliver The Kyle & Jackie O Show. Related Article Radio The ‘besties’ behind the Kyle and Jackie O reckoning He said she had told ARN: “direct contact with Mr Sandilands [was] now untenable.” McLennan said that ARN was confident in its litigation strategy. “I would like to assure shareholders that the board is committed to defending these claims and actively pursuing the cross-claims,” he said. While two key proxy advisory firms backed McLennan’s reelection, one, CGI Glass Lewis, argued Stephenson’s fixed $1.1 million contract is too much, based on the fact it is well above the median $812,000 paid to ASX250-300 companies, and ARN is not even on that list.



Hamish McLennan, chairman of ARN Media, which owns KIIS FM. Dominic Lorrimer Related Article Exclusive

Radio How KIIS cashed in on Kyle & Jackie O’s ‘explosive fights’ “This approach is notable in the context of the Company’s declining market capitalisation, which reduced from approximately $578 million at end of FY2021, to around $300 million over the following two years, and further to $124 million at FY2025 year-end and approximately $74 million as at 17 April 2026,” the report said. ARN has defended Stephenson’s pay packet based on his responsibilities and talent. The AGM is the first for Michael Stephenson, who initially joined ARN as its chief operating officer. He was previously chief sales officer at Nine (the owner of this masthead) for a decade.



This week, Sandilands and Henderson filed their defences in countersuits lodged against the duo by ARN. Sandilands’ legal team allege KIIS FM and ARN cashed in on he and Henderson’s on-air feuds, even going to lengths to promote them, a feature of the show’s daily soap opera drama. “[ARN] publicly exploited and thereby sought to monetise the conduct,” Sandilands’ lawyers said in the documents. “[They did this] without directing or requesting Mr Sandilands or Ms Henderson, not to engage in conduct of that kind.” The Business Briefing newsletter delivers major stories, exclusive coverage and expert opinion.
